newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria far right score all-time high in EU poll.
newsitem.headline: Austria far right score all-time high in EU poll.

text.p: Austria's far right scored its greatest success in a European parliamentary election on Sunday, consolidating its position as Europe's most successful nationalist party, computer projections showed.
Gloom descended on the ruling Social Democrats of Chancellor Franz Vranitzky who headed for their worst score in a nationwide election since Austria's first democratic polls in 1918.

The far-right Freedom Party led by Joerg Haider campaigned against the Maastricht treaty on European Union integration and a single currency, tapping growing disillusionment among Austrians over EU membership and sharp budget cuts.
"This is a disaster. Our credibility has slipped away," Herbert Prock, the Social Democrat leader in Tyrol, said.
The elections were held seven months after Vranitzky's government introduced a tough two-year austerity budget, which has seen cuts in welfare benefits, tax and energy price rises.

With 70 percent of the vote counted, projections had the conservative People's Party, Vranitzky's junior coalition partner in the federal government, inching ahead with 29.7 percent and the Social Democrats just behind on 29.5 percent.
The far right scored 28.2 percent, 6.3 points higher than the last test of popularity in a general election in December 1995 -- way above its target of 25 percent.
Celebrations began at the Freedom Party headquarters, with loud cheers greeting the first news of surging voter support.
"It's a great success for our party and more than a lot of us expected," said far right top EU candidate Franz Linser.
The far right emerged as the strongest party in the provinces of Salzburg and Carinthia for the first time.

Social Democrat backing plummeted 8.5 points compared to last December's score of 38 percent. Its worst result before Sunday's election was 34.9 percent in a general election in 1994 -- a far cry from its heyday in the 1970s when it won an overall majority in the national parliament.
Vranitzky's beleaguered party also looked set to lose its overall majority at Vienna city hall following a separate election for the country's most powerful regional assembly.
Austrian state television said the turnout in the EU-poll was 68 percent, far below the usual participation in national polls, reflecting possible anti-EU protests or voter apathy.
Some 5.8 million voters were eligible to vote in the first Euro-poll held in Austria to fill the 21 seats allocated to the Alpine republic in the Strasbourg-based European Parliament.

Austria joined the EU in 22 months ago following a referendum in which two-thirds of voters backed membership. But Austrians have turned their wrath on the EU, blaming membership for a series of economic ills.

Anger has risen over Austria's annual net contributions to Brussels of around 15 billion schillings ($1.5 billion), a wave of bankruptcies, company takeovers and mounting job losses amid a general economic downturn.

The Social Democrats will probably take seven seats in the European Parliament, one down on the number previously allocated to parties according to national popularity. The far right gained one to take six. The conservatives also won an extra seat giving them a total of seven.

The leftist Green party also scored well in the EU vote with 6.7 percent, up 1.9 on December's poll. They retain their one seat. The Liberal Forum party lost the only seat it had at Strasbourg after notching up only 3.5 percent, down two points.
